findings.title: parseBody() breaks after c.req.formData() was already read
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData`, do not re-derive bytes when a FormData is already cached. Minimal option: restore the pre-change line `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` and drop the arrayBuffer/bufferToFormData/bodyCache block (the case-insensitive `mediaType` guard in `parseBody` is what fixes the issue; native `Request.formData()` already accepts `Multipart/Form-Data` and `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` on Node 24 - assumption: other runtimes follow the same MIME-parsing spec). If the buffer round trip must stay, short-circuit first, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`. Add a request.test.ts case for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: Binary uploads read after `c.req.text()`/`c.req.json()`: `c.req.text()` followed by `c.req.parseBody()` on a multipart request used to throw (base: TypeError 'Content-Type was not one of ...'); at head it succeeds but file bytes are silently corrupted, because parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts:126) now rebuilds the bytes from the cached UTF-8 text. Probe: a file with bytes [255,254,0,128,65] comes back as [239,191,189,239,191,189,0,239,191,189,65]. Text-only fields are correct in this ordering.

Exact-match media type in parseBody (src/utils/body.ts:104-106) no longer accepts a comma-joined duplicate Content-Type header: with two `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` headers base returned {"foo":"bar"} and head returns {} (verified by probe). Only reachable when a client or proxy duplicates the header.
Runtime coverage: all empirical checks ran on Node v24 (undici) only; Bun, Deno, workerd and Lambda behavior of the new arrayBuffer() + Response.formData() path in parseFormData was not exercised.

parseFormData now buffers the whole body via arrayBuffer() and then copies it into a Response before parsing, where it previously called formData() on the request directly; memory behavior for large uploads was not evaluated (out of correctness scope).
testing_gaps: No test covers `c.req.formData()` (or a middleware that reads it) followed by `c.req.parseBody()` on a HonoRequest for multipart and urlencoded bodies; src/request.test.ts only covers parseBody() first and other body methods afterwards, which is why the regression above passes the suite.

No test asserts that a second body reader after parseBody()/formData() returns the same field values (existing checks at src/request.test.ts:361-364 and 378-381 only assert `not.toThrow` on an un-awaited async wrapper, so they cannot fail on wrong content or on a rejection).

findings.title: parseBody after c.req.formData() re-parses re-serialized body (CWE-436 parameter smuggling)
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), short-circuit on an existing cached FormData before touching `arrayBuffer()`, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`, and only fall through to the `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData()` path otherwise. Alternative (assumes the buffer path is not otherwise needed): restore `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()`, since native `formData()` already matches the media type case-insensitively and the `parseBody` guard change alone satisfies the issue. Add tests for `await req.formData(); await req.parseBody()` with urlencoded and multipart bodies.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- `const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()` / `const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')`

residual_risks: parseBody's new media-type check uses JS `.trim()`, which strips non-HTTP whitespace such as U+00A0, so its accept set is wider than the csrf middleware regex and the runtime's own MIME parser. Verified on Node: `Content-Type: \xa0application/x-www-form-urlencoded` skips the csrf origin check and then `parseBody()` throws a TypeError (500) where the pre-change code returned `{}`. Not a CSRF bypass on Node, and browsers cannot send that value cross-origin without a preflight; Bun/Deno/workerd FormData parsers were not testable here.

parseBody on a HonoRequest now buffers the whole body as an ArrayBuffer and keeps it in `bodyCache.arrayBuffer` alongside the parsed FormData (scratch run: bodyCache keys ["arrayBuffer","formData"]), so each form/multipart upload retains roughly twice the body size for the request lifetime compared with the previous `request.formData()` path. Matters for large uploads on routes without `bodyLimit`.

Mixed-case form media types are now parsed by `parseBody`/`validator`, but `methodOverride` still gates on lower-case `contentType?.startsWith(...)` (src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:74,92), so `_method` in an `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` body reaches the handler as an ordinary field instead of overriding the method. No exploit traced; inconsistency only.
testing_gaps: No test covers `c.req.formData()` followed by `c.req.parseBody()` on the same HonoRequest (urlencoded and multipart); this is the sequence that regressed. src/request.test.ts only covers `parseBody()` followed by other body readers.
No test covers a middleware reading the body through one accessor and the handler through `parseBody()` asserting both see the same field set (e.g. a urlencoded value containing encoded `&`/`=`).

findings.title: parseBody() after c.req.formData() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts), reuse an existing cache entry before re-reading the body, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { ...arrayBuffer + bufferToFormData path, then cache... }`. Alternative with a smaller surface: revert parseFormData to `await (request as Request).formData()` and keep only the new case-insensitive `mediaType` gate in parseBody -- on Node 24 native `Request.formData()` already parses `Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=...` and `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` (assumption: other supported runtimes follow the Fetch MIME-parsing rule too; not verifiable here). Add a regression test for `await c.req.formData()` followed by `await c.req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()   (base 97287029 line: `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()`)

residual_risks: parseBody's media-type gate changed from `startsWith` to exact match on the part before the first `;` (src/utils/body.ts:104-106). Scratch probe on Node 24: a comma-joined duplicate header `application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/x-www-form-urlencoded` parsed to {"message":"hello"} at base and now silently returns {}. Narrow (requires a client or proxy sending duplicate Content-Type headers), but it is a silent empty result rather than an error.

After `c.req.parseBody()`, `c.req.bodyCache` now holds `arrayBuffer` first and `formData` second (base: `formData` only), so `Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]` consumers -- `#cachedBody` and `cloneRawRequest` in src/request.ts -- now derive later reads from the original bytes. Probe shows this is an improvement (`parseBody()` then `text()` on a urlencoded body returns `message=hello` instead of a re-serialized multipart string, and `text()` then `parseBody()` now works instead of throwing), but it is an unannounced observable change to a public property.

Behavior of the new parse path (`new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers }).formData()` instead of native `request.formData()`) on Bun, Deno, workerd and Lambda was not exercised; those runtime suites are unavailable in this environment.
testing_gaps: No test covers `await c.req.formData()` followed by `await c.req.parseBody()` on the same HonoRequest (multipart and urlencoded); the existing validator tests only cover parseBody-then-validator and validator-then-parseBody, which is why the regression above passes the suite.

findings.title: c.req.formData() then c.req.parseBody() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), short-circuit on an existing cache entry before reading the buffer, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`. Alternatively restore the base line `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` and keep only the case-insensitive guard in `parseBody` (assumption: target runtimes parse the media type case-insensitively in native `formData()`, which was confirmed on Node 24 only). Add a regression test that calls `await req.formData()` then `await req.parseBody()` on a HonoRequest for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- `const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()` / `const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')` (base was `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()`, which returned the cached FormData)

residual_risks: `c.req.text()` followed by `c.req.parseBody()` on a multipart upload changed from throwing (base: TypeError from `new Response(text).formData()`) to succeeding with silently corrupted binary parts: a 6-byte file [255,254,0,128,13,10] came back as [239,191,189,239,191,189,0,239,191,189,13,10] in a Node 24 probe, because the ArrayBuffer is rebuilt from the UTF-8-decoded text cache (src/request.ts:228-234). Text-only fields survive. `validator('form')` already behaves this way, so this is a newly reachable variant of an existing pattern rather than a new mechanism.

`parseBody()` on a HonoRequest now leaves both `arrayBuffer` and `formData` in `bodyCache` (base cached only `formData`), so the full raw body is retained alongside the parsed FormData for the life of the request, and every repeated `parseBody()` call re-parses the buffer instead of reusing the cached FormData. Not measured; relevant for large file uploads.

Runtime coverage: all behavior was verified on Node 24 (undici) only. The switch from native `request.formData()` to `new Response(arrayBuffer).formData()` was not exercised on Bun, Deno, Workers, or Lambda, whose suites are unavailable in this environment.

`parseBody` now requires an exact media-type match instead of a prefix match, so values such as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded-foo` return `{}` where base called `formData()` and threw a TypeError. Judged benign, not explored beyond that one input.
